result.scientific_strategy:
## abd93958-a0b2-4d26-b212-96ebeb401d22 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the unchanged official two-joint-arm task. The fresh PPO baseline in experiment 1 reached 97.0% on the researcher panel and 98.0% on the protected task-reference panel at checkpoint-100352, while its endpoint regressed on both panels. Experiment 2 transferred that checkpoint and expanded training coverage to the official 6–20 cm radius range; checkpoint-100352 and its endpoint remained at 97.0% on the researcher panel and reached 98.5% on the task-reference panel. The current evidence therefore describes a near-objective policy with a fixed-panel gain but no robust cross-panel attainment, and checkpoint-100352 remains the strongest measured development policy.

**Lessons and limits:** Measured task success, rather than logged reward or training success, is the policy-progress signal. Both experiments identify checkpoint selection as important: later training reduced logged dynamics and did not improve measured success. Experiment 2 reduced the task-reference failures from four to three, recovering two short-radius negative-angle cases, but left failures at 9.4–9.9 cm and about -123 to -128 degrees plus one 18.2 cm case at -154.8 degrees. The researcher panel retained six failures across all measured experiment-2 checkpoints, each reaching the 500-step limit. The current observation representation includes errors to both valid inverse-kinematics branches, whereas the reward directly shapes Cartesian progress and hold completion; this makes angular control a plausible but untested explanation, not an established cause. Transfer compatibility is supported by the unchanged robot, action mapping, target geometry, observation semantics and network shape, but fixed 200-episode panels remain development evidence and are not the official 200-episode assessment.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved whether the residual negative-angle failures reflect insufficient joint-configuration shaping, PPO optimization dynamics, or a limitation of the transferred policy. It is also unknown whether any development-panel gain generalizes to the official final assessment.
